title: [D5 Tools] Cache-first lookup where the cache is the evidence store
summary: `ProviderTool.lookup` is cache-first: it reads a valid, unexpired record for its source, endpoint and normalized indicator out of the one store and returns it without touching the network, querying only on a miss or an expiry. The cache is the evidence store and not a second one — `sql/migrations/0017_analyst_lookup_cache.sql` adds two tables and a view in the streaming engine, in the evidence shape 0011 defined, and nothing is ever evicted. `helena.enrichment.ANALYST_TIER` now has a SQL home and a duplicated-constant test that asks the engine.
assumption_validated: That 'the cache IS the evidence store' is buildable as written rather than being a slogan over an ordinary cache — i.e. that a cache-first lookup needs no new store, no eviction, no opaque value type and no second identifier scheme. Validated: the cache entry is `EnrichmentEvidence` rows plus the retained response, the lookup key is (tenant, sensor, source, endpoint, normalized indicator), the citation identifier is the existing `evidence_id`, and the stored response is cited by the `response_version` task 34 already minted. Two secondary results, both measured rather than assumed: (1) an entry that is expired is still present and still citable, which is what makes serving it explicitly `stale` an option at all rather than a special case bolted on; (2) NEGATIVE RESULT, found by a failing test — with the endpoint out of the evidence table's primary key, two endpoints of one source that return the same bytes about one indicator mint the same `evidence_id`, and the second lookup upserted the first and handed it the other endpoint's retention. The endpoint is now in the primary key and a test holds it shut.
makes_buildable: Task 36 (budgets) has the two counters it needs already separated at the boundary: a cache hit costs a step and no live query, and `ProviderTool.lookup` is still the only place a provider is reached. Task 37 (send policy and the disclosure record) has the exact point where a disclosure row goes — the log already carries `disclosed` per call, true on a live query, false on a hit, true on a stale fallback — and `helena_reference_analyst_response` already stores the indicator AS ASKED beside the normalized key, which is the literal string a disclosure record has to name. Task 38 (the live adapter) is unchanged behind `ask(call, credential)` and now gets replay for free: the first pass spends the quota, every re-run reads the stored bytes. Task 39 (the analyst loop) gets a `ToolAnswer` whose steps already carry `cache_hit`/`live_query` and the underlying record's retrieval time, which is what a gap of kind `stale` is derived from. The increment that joins an analyst-tier claim to a finding attaches at `helena_reference_evidence_analyst`.

verification.detail: 1232 passed in 279.29 s, no skips (1186 before this task; 93 of them are tests/test_tools.py, up from 47). The new SQL is EXECUTED, not inspected: tests/test_tools.py is now an integration module end to end — an autouse fixture takes `migrated_engine`, so every tool in it writes its cache to the schema the migrations produce against a live RisingWave 3.0.3, and the cache tests assert on rows read back out of it. BYTEA round-tripping and PK-upsert idempotence were measured against a throwaway instance before the migration was written. The credential tests still load the real key from .env and assert on a boolean, never on the value.

escalations.detail: concept/08's 'whether negative results are cached'. DECIDED: YES. A `no_match` is an answer with a claim in it, not an absence, so it stores in the same shape a hit does; most lookups miss, so a hits-only cache almost never helps under a few-hundred-per-day quota; and not caching a miss re-discloses the indicator every run, which is a privacy regression in a mechanism concept/07 calls a privacy control. A FAILURE is explicitly NOT cached — an outage is not a record of what a source said, and caching one would let a five-minute outage suppress every query for the retention window. Recorded in docs/decisions/0025 §3 with the rejected variant (a shorter retention for negatives than for hits: the argument is real and unmeasured, so it would be a number chosen to look thoughtful).

concept/08's 'whether an expired entry is offered as explicitly stale when the provider is unreachable'. DECIDED: YES, as a fallback and never as a substitute for a query. The record was never evicted — that is the whole of what 'the cache is the evidence store' buys — and concept/02 defines `stale` as exactly this case. The answer carries TWO retrieval steps: a `cache_hit` citing rows that are every one of them `stale`, and a `live_query` carrying the typed failure. That required widening task 34's ToolAnswer check (see invariant_conflicts). The alternative — return the typed failure and let the analyst record a gap — is one line to reinstate and the branch is named in `ProviderTool.lookup`. Recorded in docs/decisions/0025 §4.

No second store was added and none is needed: concept/instruction.md §2 forbids 'a cache that is not itself the evidence store', and 0017's two tables are in the one streaming engine in the evidence shape 0011 defined. Stated here so the next session does not have to re-derive that this was checked. In particular there is NO in-process memoization in front of the engine read, deliberately: it would be the second store, it would make two runs in one process differ from two runs in two, and it would be invisible to a replay.

No contract field was added. `contracts.v1.RetrievalStep` already had `CACHE_HIT` waiting with nothing producing it, and it now has a producer; `retrieved_at` is populated with the underlying record's time, which is what its own docstring says it is for. `EnrichmentEvidence` still has no tier column — the `analyst` literal lives in the 0017 view exactly as `enrichment` lives in 0014's, which is the debt task 34's report recorded and this task pays.

invariant_conflicts.detail: concept/instruction.md §1 says 'no config key with one value', and this task adds `endpoint` to a layer that has exactly one endpoint today. The concept wins and the tension is recorded rather than resolved by ignoring one of them: concept/07 names the endpoint twice — in the cache key ('a valid, unexpired record for its source, endpoint and indicator') and in the retention ('retention is configured per source AND per endpoint', because a registration date never changes while a risk score moves) — and concept/ outranks instruction.md §1's generic guidance. It is not speculative machinery: there is no registry, no plugin point and no second implementation, just a required constructor argument that is part of a key. The measured endpoint/evidence_id collision (see assumption_validated) is what a single-endpoint design would have hidden until the second endpoint arrived.

Task 34's `ToolAnswer` refused any evidence beside a failure, citing concept/05 rule 4 ('a typed error, and no taxonomy object'). That check is now narrowed rather than removed: a single failure may sit beside evidence ONLY when every record is `stale`, and a failure beside an `ok` record is still refused with a test on it. The reading is that rule 4 constrains a QUERY'S OWN result, and a stale-fallback answer contains two retrievals — the failed live query, whose step carries a typed error and no taxonomy object, and the cache read, whose rows came from a query that completed days earlier and say `stale` on every one. Both are steps and both are visible, which is what keeps concept/instruction.md §2's 'never collapse stale and failed' true end to end. Task 34's stricter check was correct for a layer with no cache; this is the case it did not have. Recorded in docs/decisions/0025 §4.

Not a conflict but a discrepancy that must not be papered over (concept/instruction.md §4): Python's `str.lower` is Unicode-aware and RisingWave 3.0.3's `lower()` is ASCII-only (measured in sql/migrations/0008). So a non-ASCII U-label in uppercase folds in the Python cache key and does not in the engine's `normalized_name`. Nothing joins the two today — analyst-tier evidence is deliberately not unioned into helena_reference_evidence — and the increment that joins an analyst claim to a context owes the reconciliation. Written down in docs/decisions/0025 §2 and in the code.

deferred: PRUNING. Nothing is ever deleted, which is the point (an assessment must be able to resolve a citation however old), and nothing bounds the growth either. `helena.enrichment.prune_snapshots` is the shape it would take; what it may keep is a function of how far back replay has to reach, which concept/08 still lists as open.

A SHORTER RETENTION FOR NEGATIVES than for hits. The argument is real — an unlisted indicator may be listed tomorrow, while a listing rarely disappears — and it is unmeasured. One retention per (source, endpoint), applied to both.

THE DISCLOSURE RECORD (task 37). The log line carries `disclosed` per call and that is a local log line, not the disclosure row concept/03 asks for. The response table already stores the indicator as asked, which is the string that row has to name.
BUDGET ENFORCEMENT (task 36). A cache hit already costs no live query and nothing counts either number.

THE ANALYST TIER IN THE ENRICHED CONTEXT. helena_reference_evidence_analyst is deliberately NOT unioned into helena_reference_evidence: the tier tag would keep analyst rows out of the triage rendering, but they would still enter the enriched context of every later host that talked to the same address, which concept/03 names as the outcome the tag exists to prevent rather than one it makes safe. How an analyst claim reaches a finding is the findings increment's; the view is where it attaches.
IDN FOLDING in the cache key, and a `mailto:`-shaped (non-hierarchical) URI. Both are left unfolded on purpose — see the normalization rule — and IDN needs a dependency this project does not have.

RETENTION AS CONFIGURATION FILE VALUES. `retention_seconds` is a required constructor argument, so it is configured per (source, endpoint) by whoever builds the tool. The real numbers cannot be written yet: no live endpoint exists, and a value written from a documentation page is the error this project has corrected three times. config/*.toml is where they land when task 38 confirms the surface.
lessons: THE ENDPOINT HAS TO BE IN THE CACHE TABLE'S PRIMARY KEY, AND A TEST FOUND IT. `evidence_id` deliberately does not carry the endpoint — it is a contract shared with the enrichment tier, where there are no endpoints, and widening it would change every feed row's identity. But two endpoints of one source that return the same bytes about one indicator read the same claim out of them and mint the SAME identifier, so a key of (tenant, sensor, evidence_id) made the second lookup a silent upsert of the first, carrying the other endpoint's retention. RisingWave has no transaction around DML and an INSERT onto an existing key is an upsert, so this was invisible until a test asserted on the two retentions. A citation by evidence_id now resolves to one row per endpoint that retrieved it: the same claim, retrieved twice, which is what happened.

STATUS IS DERIVED AT READ TIME, AND THE PRECEDENT WAS ALREADY IN THE TREE. `helena.enrichment.feed_status` computes ok/stale/missing from the ledger rather than storing them, with the argument in its docstring: 'a stored stale would be wrong the moment time passed.' It is sharper for a cache, because a cached claim crosses from ok to stale with NO WRITER INVOLVED. So the cache table has retrieved_at and expires_at and no status column, and it lines up with evidence_id already excluding the status — a claim that goes stale is the same claim.

THE SAFETY RULE FOR CACHE-KEY NORMALIZATION IS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT A LIST. A fold that is too timid costs one live query and one re-disclosure of an already-disclosed indicator. A fold that is too eager serves ONE INDICATOR'S EVIDENCE FOR A DIFFERENT INDICATOR — a wrong answer with a citation on it. So: fold only what the identifier's own specification makes equivalent, and when in doubt leave the value exactly as it is. That rule is what decides the hard cases (a URL fragment stays, an IDN's two forms stay two keys, a value that will not parse is returned untouched) without needing a judgement call per case.

THE DISCLOSURE MEASUREMENT IS THE ADAPTER, NOT A COUNTER. `helena.tools` imports no HTTP machinery at all (asserted off the module's own AST, task 34's test), so the injected adapter is the ONLY thing in the layer that can reach a provider. An adapter that was not called is therefore an indicator that was not sent, which turns 'a cache hit discloses nothing' into a property a test can hold rather than a sentence in a docstring.

STORING THE RESPONSE BEFORE EVALUATING IT IS LOAD-BEARING, AND THE MALFORMED CASE IS WHAT PROVES IT. A response that will not map into the declared subset ends up on disk under its digest with NO claims beside it. Two things fall out for free: the operator can investigate the failure against what actually arrived, and the next lookup is still a miss — because the cache read requires at least one claim, a stored-but-unmappable response can never be served as an answer.

MAKING A DEPENDENCY REQUIRED IN A 40-TEST MODULE COSTS ONE AUTOUSE FIXTURE, NOT 40 SIGNATURES. `ProviderTool` takes a required `cache`, because 'every provider tool is cache-first' and an optional one is a tool that is not. tests/test_tools.py gained `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration`, an autouse fixture that pushes `migrated_engine` onto a module-level handle, and one line in the `tool()` builder. `migrated_engine` empties data tables rather than re-migrating, so 47 unit tests becoming integration tests cost about 20 s, not minutes.

RISINGWAVE 3.0.3 BYTEA ROUND-TRIPS EXACTLY, INCLUDING NUL AND INVALID UTF-8, and psycopg returns `memoryview` — `bytes(row[0])` is needed before comparing. Measured before the migration was written, which is why the retained response is BYTEA and not TEXT: an encoding guess at the store boundary would be a re-encoding nobody recorded, on the one payload that exists to be compared against what the provider actually sent.
failed_approaches: Putting the cache in a module of its own (`src/helena/cache.py`). Backed out before it was written: tests/test_package_layout.py requires every module to be a named architecture component or a named support module, and 'cache' is neither — concept/03 lists cache-first lookup as a RESPONSIBILITY of the provider-tool component, not as a component. Adding it would have meant inventing a category to hold one file. It is in helena/tools.py, which is where concept/03 puts it.

Unioning helena_reference_evidence_analyst into helena_reference_evidence, the way 0014 unions the feeds. Rejected: the enrichment-tier view feeds helena_analytical_enriched_context, which is what triage is rendered from. The tier allow-list would keep analyst rows out of the RENDERING, but they would still be joined into the enriched context of every later host that talked to the same address — the outcome concept/03 says the tier tag exists to prevent. tests/test_rendering.py's 'DISTINCT evidence_tier is only enrichment' assertion would also have quietly stopped meaning what it says.

Adding the endpoint to `helena.enrichment.evidence_id`. That is 'changing a contract's identity' under concept/instruction.md §3, it has a second home in sql/migrations/0014 that tests/test_mapping.py asserts equal by execution, and it would have changed every feed row's identifier for a distinction feeds do not have. The endpoint went into the cache table's primary key instead.

Filtering expired entries inside `EvidenceCache.read`. It reads more naturally and it collapses a miss into an expiry: the caller needs both, because a miss means 'query' and an expiry means 'query, and fall back to this record if the query does not complete'. Filtering there would have made the record that could be served explicitly stale one nobody knew was there — the exact collapse concept/instruction.md §2 forbids, arriving as a tidier function.
next_session_should_know: Task 36 is budgets and this task built the thing budgets are counted over. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE CALL IS NOW `ProviderTool(source_id=..., endpoint='<logical-name>', credential=..., ask=<adapter>, cache=EvidenceCache(connection), retention_seconds=<int>, logger=..., redactor=...)`. `endpoint` and `retention_seconds` are required and have no defaults, `endpoint` must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_]*$ (it reaches the tool name the model is shown, so it is not a path and never a URL), and the tool's name is now `lookup_<source>_<endpoint>`. (2) A CACHE HIT COSTS A STEP AND NO LIVE QUERY, which is the distinction concept/07 says the two budgets have to be set against each other over — 'a budget that seems generous for a model call is not survivable for a handful of provider lookups'. The two numbers are countable off `RetrievalStep.outcome` without adding anything. (3) THE STALE FALLBACK IS AN ANSWER WITH TWO STEPS AND ONE OF THEM IS A FAILURE. Anything that walks `ToolAnswer.steps` assuming a failure means no evidence is wrong now; `ToolAnswer.failure` still returns the typed error and `record.status` is `stale` on every served row. (4) `missing` STILL HAS NO PRODUCER AT THIS LAYER AND MUST NOT GET ONE FROM A CACHE MISS. A miss is the reason to query, not an absence of a source; recording it as `missing` is the collapse concept/instruction.md §2 forbids wearing an optimisation's clothes. (5) TESTS/TEST_TOOLS.PY IS AN INTEGRATION MODULE NOW. `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration`, an autouse `_store` fixture takes `migrated_engine` and pushes it onto `_ENGINE`, and `cache()`/`tool()` read it. If you add a test there it gets an engine whether it wants one or not. (6) NOTHING IS EVICTED AND NOTHING PRUNES. Both cache tables grow without bound, on purpose (see docs/decisions/0025 §1) and with no bound. If a later increment wants one, the shape is `enrichment.prune_snapshots` and the retention horizon is an open question in concept/08, not a number to pick. (7) THE STAND-IN ADAPTER STILL CLAIMS NOTHING ABOUT THE HUNTING API'S ENVELOPE. That is still task 38's to confirm against the artifact, and it is still the mistake concept/05 records most emphatically.
